subject: Large Hadron Collider
title: Physicists Finally Turned Lead Into Gold. It Lasted a Microsecond

scenes.text: Alchemists failed for centuries. Physicists finally turned lead into gold.
It happened inside the Large Hadron Collider, a 27-kilometer ring under France and Switzerland.
Lead nuclei race past each other at almost the speed of light, without even touching.
Their electric fields can knock out three protons. Lead minus three protons is gold.
From 2015 to 2018, that made about 86 billion gold atoms.
Total weight: 29 trillionths of a gram. And each atom fell apart in about a millionth of a second.

description:
In 2025, CERN's ALICE experiment reported measuring lead turning into gold at the Large Hadron Collider.
When lead nuclei narrowly miss each other, their electromagnetic fields can knock out three protons, turning lead (82 protons) into gold (79 protons).
Across the LHC's 2015 to 2018 run, about 86 billion gold nuclei were made, about 29 picograms in total, and most lasted around a microsecond.
If you could make real gold this way, would it ever be worth the cost?
first_comment: At its peak, the collider was making about 89,000 gold nuclei every second, and it still added up to almost nothing. How long do you think it would take to make one gold ring?
